question: Should OpenClaw accept Android device-control, ADB-style access, or dynamic code execution from connected Android nodes, and should those high-power pieces route through Android-specific commands or the generic node-hosted tool contract?
rationale: The remaining request changes phone authority, sensitive-data access, and model-visible execution boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security shape.

options.title: Split and gate Android authority
options.body: Implement only narrow Android device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

options.title: Route through node-hosted tools
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8287 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90431 as the core contract before Android exposes ADB or dynamic execution descriptors.

options.title: Keep high-power execution out of core
options.body: Reject ADB and dynamic Android code execution in OpenClaw core for now and require an external plugin, ClawHub package, or app-specific fork for that authority.

recommendation.title: Split and gate Android authority
recommendation.body: Implement only narrow Android device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current routing signal for the generic node-to-model tool contract is the open candidate PR and related Gateway/node/tool history under this account.
